Storage, beds and lamps

Storage furniture keeps your things where you live, beds give you somewhere to lie down, and lamps light a room without fuel. All of them are built from furniture plans.

Updated 8 November 2026 · 7 min read · Everyone · feature ledger · all guides

Before you start

Every piece here is built from a furniture plan. In Survival, carry a Furniture hammer, open E > Build, pick the plan and its woods and check the Need / have counts; the materials are spent only when the piece is placed, and Creative placement is free. Press R to turn the ghost and right click to place it. See Furniture and carpentry for placing, turning and moving furniture.

Costs below are in carried pieces, the same counts that Need / have shows. Each part uses the wood you choose for it, and parts that share a wood add up. Floor pieces need a solid block under every foot, and wall pieces need solid wall behind them: leaves, plants, doors and chests do not count, and nothing here can stand on other furniture.

To use a piece, put the plan and any tool away first (B puts the furniture tool away), stand within 6 m of the whole piece, aim at it and right click. The Cooking stove is a furniture plan too; cooking on it is covered in Crafting and recipes.

Using furniture storage

Wardrobes, chests of drawers, the bookcase and the kitchen pieces with storage all work the same way. Each piece has its own storage, holding up to 250 capacity and 64 kinds of item whatever woods it is made from.

  1. Put the plan and any tool away and aim at the piece. The hint reads, for example, Wardrobe | RMB open wardrobe storage.
  2. Right click. The storage panel opens with your pack on the left (Pack > click to store) and the stored items on the right, with the capacity used, for example Wardrobe: 12.0 / 250.
  3. Click an item to move one across. Shift + click moves as many as fit.
  4. Close the inventory when you are done. Walking out of reach also closes the storage.

A new kind of item is refused once 64 kinds are stored (Furniture storage holds at most 64 kinds of items), and a move is refused when the other side is full (No transfer: destination is full or item is unavailable). Moving a piece keeps everything inside it.

Careful. Empty a storage piece before you take it up. The game says, for example, Empty the wardrobe before removing it or Empty the drawers before removing them.

Wardrobes and chests of drawers

  • Wardrobe (Wardrobe plan): 1 m wide, 2 m tall and 0.5 m deep, with two doors. It costs 5 board pieces: 3 for the Body, 1 for the Front (both doors) and 1 for the Fittings (handles).
  • Chest of drawers (Chest of drawers plan, shown as Drawers on its tile): 1 m wide, 1 m tall and 0.5 m deep, with three drawers. It costs 4 board pieces: 2 Body, 1 Front (all three drawer fronts) and 1 Fittings.
  • Both stand on four feet. Right click either one to open its storage, as described above.

While the storage is open, the wardrobe doors swing open and the top drawer slides out. This happens only on your screen and only when the space in front is clear: a block, a door, other furniture or you standing there keeps them shut. With Reduce motion on, they appear open straight away. The movement is only for show; the storage works either way. Wardrobes and chests of drawers

Kitchen cupboards and counters

Five kitchen plans have storage: the open Kitchen counter, the Counter cabinet, the Sink cabinet, the Kitchen cupboard and the Wall cupboard. They share the same storage panel, titled Kitchen storage. Kitchen storage and cupboards

  • Kitchen cupboard: a floor cupboard 1 m square and 1 m high with two doors; its top lines up with counters and sinks. Choose Body (body and top), Fronts (the two doors) and Fittings (handles). It costs 5 board pieces: 4 Body and 1 Fronts.
  • Wall cupboard (Kitchen wall cupboard plan): 1 m wide, 0.75 m high and 0.5 m deep. It costs 3 board pieces: 2 Body and 1 Fronts. Aim at a wall side and press R until its back faces the wall. Four full solid wall pieces must cover its back; it needs no floor.
  • The handles use the Body wood until you choose a Fittings wood. Choosing one adds 1 board piece to either cupboard.
  • On a Sink cabinet, aim at the lower cabinet to open its storage. Aiming at the basin uses nearby fresh water instead.
  • Both cupboards' doors swing open on your screen while the storage is open, under the same rules as the wardrobe.
Careful. Empty a cupboard or counter before taking it up (Empty the kitchen cupboard before removing it, Empty the kitchen counter before removing it). You cannot remove a block that holds up furniture, including the wall behind a wall cupboard or shelf: Take up the furniture before removing its support.

Bookcase and wall shelf

  • Bookcase (Bookcase plan): an open bookcase 1 m wide, 1.5 m tall and 0.5 m deep, with three shelves. It costs 3 board pieces: 2 Frame and 1 Panel (shelves and top). Right click its body to open Bookcase storage; stored items do not show on the shelves.
  • Wall shelf (Wall shelf plan): one shelf board on two brackets, 1 m wide, 0.5 m deep and 0.5 m high. It costs 2 board pieces: 1 Frame (brackets) and 1 Panel (shelf). Aim at a wall side and press R until its back faces the wall; two full solid wall pieces must be behind it. It has no storage.

Both can show one red lantern on top. Bookcase and wall shelf

  1. Select a red lantern, aim at the top of the bookcase or at the shelf and right click. The hint reads RMB place display. In Survival this uses one carried lantern; in Creative it is free.
  2. To take the lantern back, select an empty hotbar slot, aim at the lantern and right click (RMB take display). You get a lantern back only if one was paid for it.
  3. Press Ctrl + Z to undo the last display change.

The space above the top must be clear (Clear the space above the tabletop first). With a lantern in place you can still open the bookcase storage by aiming at its body, and you can move either piece. Take the lantern off before changing the woods or taking the piece up: Take the top display before restyling or taking up this bookcase, or Take the shelf display before restyling or taking up this shelf.

Beds and resting

  • Single bed (Single bed plan): 1 m wide, 2 m long and 0.875 m high, with one place to lie. It costs 3 board pieces of the Frame wood and 4 Wool.
  • Double bed (Double bed plan): 2 m wide and 2 m long, with two places side by side. It costs 6 board pieces and 7 Wool.
  • Bedding comes in Cream, Sage or Rust. Every colour uses ordinary Wool from sheep.
  1. Put the plan away. Stand on dry, solid ground beside the bed, within 2 m of the middle of a place to lie. In Creative, land first: you cannot rest while flying.
  2. Aim at the bed (the hint reads, for example, Single bed | RMB rest) and right click. You lie down in the nearest free place.
  3. Press Space or right click to get up. You stand at a clear, supported spot beside the bed.
Key or actionWhat it does
Right click a bedLie down (plan put away, within 2 m)
Space or Right click, while restingGet up when the way out is clear

The bed needs solid ground under all its legs, room for your whole body on top and a clear, supported way between you and the bed. Otherwise the game says why, for example Move within 2 m of a resting position, The bed needs clear room for your whole body or The bed needs a clear, supported approach and exit. While you rest you can look around and open your inventory; other actions wait until you stand up. Beds and resting

If the way out is blocked when you try to get up, you stay lying down: Bed exit blocked | Make room to stand safely. You also get up on your own if the bed is moved, changed or loses its support, if something fills the space you lie in, or if something pushes you.

Good to know. Resting in a bed is optional and is only a pose. It does not pass time or skip the night, it does not heal, feed or water you, and your Survival needs carry on as normal. It does not set your Home or respawn point: for that, use Rest / set respawn at your Home crate (Resting and setting your respawn point).

Nobody can move, take up or change a bed while someone lies in it (Leave the bed before changing it; on a server, Bed occupied | Ask the resting player to leave first). If you save while lying down, the save puts you upright beside the bed. If the way out is blocked, the save is refused (Bed exit blocked; cannot save an embedded player) until you clear it.

Lamps and light

  • Floor lamp (Floor lamp plan): 0.5 m square and 1.6875 m tall.
  • Table lamp (Table lamp plan): the same base and lantern on a short stem, 0.5 m square and 0.875 m tall.
  • Wall lamp (Wall lamp plan): the same lantern on a wooden backplate and bracket that hangs on a wall. It is 0.5 m wide and 0.75 m high, and reaches 0.75 m out from the wall. Wall lamp
  • Each costs one Red lantern plus 2 board pieces: 1 Frame and 1 Panel. On the floor and table lamps the Frame wood makes the feet and stem; on the wall lamp it makes the backplate and bracket. The Panel wood makes the base and top. Red lanterns are crafted; see Crafting and recipes.
  • The floor and table lamps stand on four feet, so each foot needs a solid block under it. The table lamp is meant for a counter or ledge built from blocks. It cannot stand on furniture, so not on a furniture table, desk or kitchen counter.
  • Taking up a lamp you paid for returns its lantern and boards, if your pack has room.

Hang a wall lamp

  1. Select the Wall lamp plan and aim at the side of a wall, not its top. The workbench hint reads Wall side | R turns back | RMB on/off.
  2. Press R until the back of the ghost faces the wall. Until it does, the game says Aim at a wall side; R turns the back toward it.
  3. Right click to hang it. Four full solid wall pieces must be behind it; leaves, plants, doors and chests do not count. Otherwise the game says The furniture needs a complete solid wall behind it. The lamp needs no floor.

You cannot remove a block that holds up a wall lamp (Take up the furniture before removing its support). To move it, select any furniture plan, lock the lamp with Shift + left click, aim at another wall side, turn its back to the wall with R and right click.

Switch a lamp on or off

  1. Put the plan and any tool away; an empty hand works.
  2. Aim at the lamp. The hint shows its state, for example Floor lamp | On | RMB switch off or Wall lamp | Off | RMB switch on.
  3. Right click to switch it off or on.

A new lamp starts switched on. The setting is saved with the world, and a lamp needs no fuel or power. Switching is not an undo step. Floor and table lamps

A lamp that is on lights the walls, floor and ceiling around it with the same warm light as a placed red lantern; a switched-off lamp's lantern stops glowing. A red lantern on display on a table, desk, bookcase or wall shelf lights its surroundings in the same way. The game draws light from at most 16 nearby light sources at a time, so in a room full of lights some may add none.

On a server

  • Storage: opening a piece asks the server for its contents (Opening furniture storage | waiting for server), and each move waits for the server too. You can only use storage where you are allowed to build, not on another player's plot. If the panel says Furniture storage waits for pack confirmation, open it again to refresh. In Creative, the left list shows your carried supplies.
  • Displays: putting a lantern on display or taking it back waits for the server to confirm your stock (RMB place display | Server confirms stock).
  • Beds: right click, then wait for the server to confirm (Waiting for the server to confirm bed use). Other players see you lying down, and two players can share a double bed. A place someone already uses is refused: That resting position is occupied.
  • A blocked way out: on a dedicated server you cannot eat while you lie in a bed, or sit on a seat, whose way out is blocked: Eating refused: Make room to stand up before eating | food kept. Clear the space first; the food stays in your pack.
  • Hosting: if you host the world and lie in a bed whose way out gets blocked, saving and Stop hosting wait until you can stand up beside the bed. Other players can still dig, build and move furniture meanwhile, so the space can be cleared. Then try again.
  • Lamps: wall lamps work on a server like the other lamps. Switching waits for the server. Switch a lamp on before taking it up: Switch the lamp on before taking it up; history keeps its power.
  • Changing woods: storage pieces and the wall shelf can change materials on a server; beds and lamps cannot (This furniture does not support material changes on servers).
  • Opening doors and drawers are drawn only on your own screen; other players see the piece closed.
